editorialRead.oneLineSummary: OpenHands/OpenHands leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 26 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 26 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.

editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit whether a refreshed Codex cloud configuration applies to your current session
dailyInsight.insight: Codex's fresh cloud-configuration change supports a narrow audit for teams that rely on managed configuration: do not assume a background refresh changes an already-running session. The inspected source says the old path warmed disk while new sessions in the same process retained the startup snapshot; the proposed implementation reloads the shared bundle for later configuration loads and keeps the last successful bundle when a refresh fails.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The public change makes CloudConfigBundleLoader retrieve the latest shared bundle on each configuration load, updates the in-memory bundle only after a successful refresh, and cancels refresh work when its loader is replaced or its final clone is dropped. Its focused tests cover refreshed requirements and managed configuration in later sessions, concurrent initial loads, failure and recovery, clearing, and refresh-task cancellation.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Configuration controls can look live while a long-running agent process is still acting on an earlier policy bundle. Knowing the session boundary lets an operator verify a sensitive change deliberately instead of assuming a background fetch changed the next tool decision in place.

actions.audience: Operator responsible for managed Codex configuration
actions.label: Test the session boundary in a disposable environment
actions.instruction: In a disposable managed configuration environment, make one harmless configuration change, allow the documented refresh path to run, then compare one already-running session with a newly started session. Record which session sees the revised requirement and keep existing approval or review controls in place; do not use the test to weaken a policy boundary.

receipts.title: Apply refreshed cloud config bundles to later sessions
receipts.supports: Shows the stated old startup-snapshot behavior, the reload and last-successful-bundle design, cancellation paths, and focused tests for later sessions and refresh failure recovery.

confidence.basis: One fresh public Codex commit and its inspected source-level test additions agree on the narrow later-session and failure-recovery mechanism, but the receipt alone does not establish deployment or every configuration topology.

dailyInsight.limitation: The commit and tests show intended source behavior, not a released deployment, the exact refresh cadence of a managed environment, or behavior across every client, cache, and policy configuration.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a public regression shows that an already-running session receives the refreshed bundle through a different path, a later session still retains the startup snapshot after a successful refresh, or the change is reverted or materially redesigned.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for release documentation or public integration coverage that names the configuration-refresh boundary and verifies it against a running managed session; that would determine how directly operators can rely on this source change.
